readme:
# self-learn — a Hermes-style self-learning loop, packaged as a Claude Code plugin

A native port of [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)'s
self-improvement loop, built from the design lessons of two prior-art Claude Code
plugins ([BayramAnnakov/claude-reflect](https://github.com/BayramAnnakov/claude-reflect),
[UniM0cha/claude-self-improving-skills](https://github.com/UniM0cha/claude-self-improving-skills)).

This repo packages that loop as a **plugin**: the subagents, slash commands, and
edit-safety hooks install through Claude Code's plugin system; the one piece a
plugin cannot provide — an out-of-band background scheduler — self-registers on
first session against whatever scheduler the host OS provides.

## Quick install

Run entirely from a shell (no Claude session needed — the `claude` CLI does the
plugin steps):

```
claude plugin marketplace add secondfry/claude-code-self-learn
claude plugin install self-learn@secondfry-self-learn
```

Restart any running Claude Code session to pick up the plugin's hooks/agents/commands.
The SessionStart hook then self-registers the background dispatcher against the
host OS scheduler automatically — **no extra step on any platform**.
See [Install](#install) below for what that registration does and local-dev variants.

> **Platform support:** macOS, Linux, and Windows. The hooks run through Node
> (present wherever Claude Code runs from an npm/fnm install) and the dispatcher
> is pure Python 3. The scheduler self-registers per OS: a launchd LaunchAgent on
> macOS, a `systemd --user` timer (cron fallback) on Linux, and a Scheduled Task
> on Windows. Requirements: **Node** on `PATH` (for the hooks) and **Python 3**
> (`python3`/`py`) for the pipeline.

> **Model note:** the shipped default `learn_model` is `claude-sonnet-4-6`
> (Claude Sonnet 4.6), a public Anthropic API model id — the learners run
> against it out of the box. Override it in `~/.claude/self-learn/config.json`
> to run on a different model (see [Configuration](#configuration)); if you
> point `learn_gateway` at a proxy, keep the id format coupled to that gateway.

## How it differs from Hermes / Odysseus (and why)

Both reference systems own their agent loop, so they learn **inline and live** —
Hermes mirrors every turn into memory on a background thread; Odysseus writes via
a `manage_memory` tool call mid-turn. A Claude Code plugin **cannot** hook the
turn loop, so that path is closed to us. Instead our substrate is the transcript
JSONL that Claude Code already writes to disk, and learning runs **out-of-band**.

The trigger design copies the one out-of-band mechanism both references DO have:

- **Idle-gate** (Hermes' curator, ≥2h idle): only process a transcript whose file
  has been untouched for `SL_IDLE_MIN` minutes ⇒ the session is finished. No
  partial reads; native Auto-memory (which writes live) finished long ago, so we
  never race it.
- **Watermark counter** (Odysseus' event-threshold): a per-transcript record of
  the msg/tool-call totals at last processing. Reprocess only when enough NEW
  work has landed. The watermark IS the bookkeeping.

## Compared to claude-reflect

[claude-reflect](https://github.com/BayramAnnakov/claude-reflect) is the closest
widely-used prior art. Both learn from the history Claude Code already writes;
the core bets differ.

| | **self-learn** | [claude-reflect](https://github.com/BayramAnnakov/claude-reflect) |
|---|---|---|
| Learns | **facts + skills** | corrections (facts) + skill discovery |
| Fact store | native Auto-memory (`memory/*.md` + `MEMORY.md`) | `CLAUDE.md` hierarchy |
| Trigger | **out-of-band scheduler**, idle-gated | auto capture hook + manual `/reflect` |
| In-session cost | **none** — runs headless, out of process | a review turn when you run `/reflect` |
| Human in the loop | no (auto-managed, rollback-guarded) | yes — you approve each learning |
| Skill-edit safety | snapshot → validate → rollback | — |
| Lifecycle curator | yes | — |
| Platforms | macOS, Linux, Windows | macOS, Linux, Windows |

**The distinguishing bet is *fully* out-of-band.** claude-reflect captures
corrections live and applies them when you run `/reflect`, keeping a human review
step. self-learn instead processes finished transcripts on a scheduler, so
learning **never occupies or bills an interactive turn** — and it writes Claude
Code's **native Auto-memory** format for facts while *also* distilling skills. The
trade is the review gate for zero in-session cost and automatic skill distillation.

The wider field (e.g. [claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem),
[agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory)) mostly builds memory as an
MCP server with RAG-style retrieval injected at session start; self-learn
deliberately runs no MCP server and adds nothing to the live context — it writes
the native on-disk format Claude Code already reads.

## Division of labor

- **Facts (declarative memory)** → the **fact-extractor** subagent writes Claude
  Code's **native Auto-memory format** (one file per fact + `MEMORY.md` index).
  It routes by scope: cross-project `user`/`feedback` facts go to the global
  store `~/.claude/memory/`; `project`/`reference` facts to the per-project
  `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/memory/`.
- **Skills (procedures)** → the **skill-distiller** subagent: turn a session's
  proven technique into a reusable `SKILL.md`, then curate those skills over time.

## The loop

```
  ┌─ OS scheduler every ~1800s (launchd / systemd / Scheduled Task)┐
  │ self-learn-dispatcher → pipeline/dispatch.py                  │
  └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                   ▼
  ┌─ dispatch.py (OUT OF SESSION) ────────────────────────────────┐
  │ scan ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl                            │
  │  idle-gate: file mtime older than SL_IDLE_MIN → finished      │
  │  watermark: new user-msgs / tool-calls since last pass        │
  │   FACT  branch: new real-user-msgs >= SL_BATCH_MSGS           │
  │   SKILL branch: new tool-calls >= SL_DISTILL_THRESHOLD         │
  │                 AND file-edits >= SL_MIN_FILE_EDITS           │
  │  cap SL_MAX_PER_PASS learner invocations per pass (drain)     │
  │  then poke curator.py --auto (internally interval-gated)      │
  └───────────────┬──────────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
     claude -p --agent fact-extractor    claude -p --agent skill-distiller
     --permission-mode auto (classifier-gated)  --add-dir ~/.claude/{projects,skills,memory}
                  │                             │
                  ▼                             ▼
  ┌─ fact-extractor subagent ────┐  ┌─ skill-distiller subagent ─────────┐
  │ dedup vs MEMORY.md → update  │  │ patch existing → umbrella → add    │
  │ or create <type>_<slug>.md   │  │ ref file → create new (last resort)│
  │ (native format). Routes by   │  │ Class-level names only. Skips      │
  │ scope. Never secrets.        │  │ one-offs.                          │
  └──────────────┬───────────────┘  └───────────────┬────────────────────┘
     writes memory/*.md (global or proj) writes ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
                  │                                  │
                  ▼                                  ▼
  ┌─ PreToolUse backup + PostToolUse validate (Write|Edit|MultiEdit) ┐
  │ backup_skill.py: snapshot SKILL.md before edit.             │
  │ validate_skill.py: SKILL.md → validate → ROLL BACK if broken │
  │ → stamp provenance → record patch. memory/*.md → ADVISORY.   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ Stop hook (run.mjs → analyze_turn.py) — telemetry only ─────────┐
  │ records skill use/view per stop for the curator's idle clock     │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Code vs. state (the plugin split)

- **Code** lives in this plugin (`pipeline/`, `hooks/`, `agents/`, `commands/`,
  `scheduler/`). It is stateless and relocatable — every internal reference is
  resolved relative to the file (`__file__`) or `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.
- **Mutable state** lives in `~/.claude/self-learn/` and is NEVER written into the
  plugin repo: `state.json` (skill telemetry + per-transcript watermarks), the
  dispatcher log, `skill_backups/`, the learners' scratch `agent-cwd/`, and the
  lock/flag files. The Python resolves these via `~/.claude/self-learn` regardless
  of where the plugin is installed, so updating or moving the plugin never
  disturbs accumulated state.

## Layout

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Plugin manifest |
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | Local marketplace entry (single-plugin) |
| `agents/{fact-extractor,skill-distiller}.md` | The two learner subagents |
| `commands/*.md` | `/distill-skill`, `/extract-facts`, `/curator-status`, `/prune-skills`, `/archive-skill`, `/restore-skill`, `/pin-skill` |
| `hooks/hooks.json` | Wires the 4 hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) in exec form (`command: node`) — no shell dependency |
| `hooks/run.mjs` | Cross-platform launcher: pipes hook stdin to a Python pipeline script, fail-safe |
| `hooks/session-init.mjs` | SessionStart: self-register the OS scheduler + run the throttled curator |
| `hooks/lib/py.mjs` | Per-OS Python 3 interpreter resolution (`python3`/`py`/`python`) |
| `pipeline/dispatch.py` | **The out-of-band loop.** Scan → idle/watermark gate → invoke learners headlessly → poke curator. `--seed` marks the existing backlog as already-considered |
| `pipeline/curator.py` | Skill lifecycle state machine + CLI |
| `pipeline/analyze_turn.py` | Stop-hook: skill use/view telemetry only (no nudges) |
| `pipeline/backup_skill.py` | PreToolUse: snapshot SKILL.md before edit |
| `pipeline/validate_skill.py` | PostToolUse: SKILL.md validate → rollback → stamp provenance → record patch; memory/*.md advisory format check |
| `pipeline/lib/transcript.py` | JSONL transcript parser + `is_real_user_msg` noise filter |
| `pipeline/lib/store.py` | Atomic state store (flock on POSIX, msvcrt on Windows): per-skill telemetry + per-transcript watermarks (writes `~/.claude/self-learn/state.json`) |
| `scheduler/install.mjs` | Cross-platform scheduler installer: renders + registers a launchd LaunchAgent (macOS), `systemd --user` timer/cron (Linux), or Scheduled Task (Windows). Idempotent + self-healing |

## Install

[Quick install](#quick-install) is the whole happy path. This section covers the
variants: local development and how the scheduler self-registers.

**Local development** (run straight from a checkout, no marketplace):

```
claude --plugin-dir /path/to/claude-code-self-learn
```

**Scheduler.** Nothing to wire by hand on any platform — the SessionStart hook
(`hooks/session-init.mjs`) calls `scheduler/install.mjs`, which registers the
dispatcher for the host OS and refreshes it (idempotently) each session:

| OS | Backend | Registered at |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | launchd LaunchAgent | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ru.secondfry.self-learn.plist` |
| Linux | `systemd --user` timer (cron fallback) | `~/.config/systemd/user/self-learn.timer` |
| Windows | Scheduled Task | `self-learn-dispatcher` (Task Scheduler) |

Each backend runs `pipeline/dispatch.py` ~every 30 min from the plugin's **cache**
copy (so it survives the source tree moving), using the absolute Python resolved
at install. To force a registration outside a session: `node
/path/to/claude-code-self-learn/scheduler/install.mjs`.

The existing transcript backlog is **learned from, not abandoned**: the loop
drains it **oldest-first** (chronological, so a later session's fact corrects an
earlier one — never the reverse), `SL_MAX_PER_PASS` transcripts per pass. Trigger
a pass immediately — macOS: `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/ru.secondfry.self-learn`;
Linux: `systemctl --user start self-learn.service`; Windows: `schtasks /Run /TN self-learn-dispatcher`.

To skip the backlog and only learn from new work, run this ONCE before installing:
`python3 /path/to/claude-code-self-learn/pipeline/dispatch.py --seed`.

## Configuration

Every tunable lives in **`~/.claude/self-learn/config.json`** — one
human-editable file, read fresh each pass, so changing the model or thresholds
takes effect on the next 30-min run with **no scheduler reload**. The file is
optional; every key has a built-in default. Each key can also be set by an
`SL_*` env var, and **precedence is env var > config.json > default** — env vars
stay useful for a one-off shell override or a scheduler-baked tweak. The
`self-learn-config` skill (shipped with the plugin) guides edits to this file.

| key | env var | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dispatch_enabled` | `SL_DISPATCH` | `true` | `false` disables the whole out-of-band loop |
| `facts_enabled` | `SL_FACT_NUDGE` | `true` | `false` disables the fact-extraction branch |
| `skills_enabled` | `SL_SKILL_NUDGE` | `true` | `false` disables the skill-distillation branch |
| `idle_min` | `SL_IDLE_MIN` | `30` | Debounce: minutes a transcript must be idle before it's "finished" |
| `batch_msgs` | `SL_BATCH_MSGS` | `1` | Min NEW user messages since watermark → fact pass (1 = any) |
| `distill_threshold` | `SL_DISTILL_THRESHOLD` | `1` | Min NEW tool calls since watermark → skill pass (1 = any) |
| `min_file_edits` | `SL_MIN_FILE_EDITS` | `1` | Min file edits for a skill pass (1 = any real work) |
| `max_per_pass` | `SL_MAX_PER_PASS` | `8` | Max learner invocations per dispatcher pass (backlog drain rate) |
| `agent_timeout` | `SL_AGENT_TIMEOUT` | `600` | Per-subagent wall-clock ceiling (seconds) |
| `learn_model` | `SL_LEARN_MODEL` | `claude-sonnet-4-6` | Model id passed via `--model` (format is gateway-coupled — see below) |
| `learn_gateway` | `SL_LEARN_GATEWAY` | `""` | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` for the headless runs only. Empty = use the gateway from settings.json. |
| `learn_token_env` | `SL_LEARN_TOKEN_ENV` | `""` | Name of the env var holding the upstream gateway's auth token (the token itself is never stored in config.json). |
| `claude_bin` | `SL_CLAUDE_BIN` | (auto) | Override the resolved `claude` binary path |
| `stale_after_days` | `SL_STALE_AFTER_DAYS` | `30` | Curator: idle days → mark a skill stale |
| `archive_after_days` | `SL_ARCHIVE_AFTER_DAYS` | `90` | Curator: idle days → archive (×2 if use_count≥3) |
| `curate_interval_days` | `SL_CURATE_INTERVAL_DAYS` | `7` | Curator: min days between auto-curate passes |
| `curate_min_skills` | `SL_CURATE_MIN_SKILLS` | `5` | Curator: min agent-distilled skills before auto-curate acts |

### Model ↔ gateway coupling

The model id format depends on which upstream gateway the headless runs hit —
they must be set as a pair:

- `learn_gateway: "https://your-gateway.example.com/raw/anthropic"` →
  `learn_model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"` (bare id)
- `learn_gateway: "https://your-gateway.example.com/raw/openrouter"` →
  `learn_model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"` (vendor-prefixed)

Leaving `learn_gateway` empty routes learner traffic through whatever gateway
`claude` loads from `~/.claude/settings.json`. If that is a local/proxy gateway
that rewrites aliases to a fixed backing model, a specific `learn_model` may be
silently rewritten. To hit a specific real upstream model, set `learn_gateway`
to bypass it for learner traffic only — interactive sessions are untouched. The
auth token is read at run time from the
env var named by `learn_token_env`; it is never written into config.json.

## Permissions — explicit auto-mode

Each headless learner runs with `--permission-mode auto`: the auto-mode
classifier approves/denies every action non-interactively. This is REQUIRED —
`~/.claude/**` is a "sensitive directory" that Claude Code hard-blocks tool-based
writes to under `acceptEdits`, even with `--add-dir` or an explicit `Write(...)`
allow-rule. Auto-mode is the classifier-governed path that permits a legitimate
memory/skill write into the user's own dirs while still gating unsafe actions.
`--permission-mode bypassPermissions` is deliberately NOT used. Nothing is added
to the interactive session's `permissions.allow`; normal sessions are unaffected.

## Design invariants (why it won't misbehave)

- **Never wedges a session.** The Stop hook only records telemetry and always
  approves. Learning happens out-of-process; a crash there can't touch your work.
- **Never races native Auto-memory.** The idle-gate guarantees we only read
  finished transcripts, hours after native memory wrote live.
- **Never re-processes.** The watermark advances once a batch is considered.
- **Never abandons the backlog.** Existing transcripts are drained oldest-first
  and learned from; nothing is skipped by default.
- **Never bursts.** `SL_MAX_PER_PASS` caps invocations per pass.
- **Never deletes.** Archiving moves skill dirs to `~/.claude/skills/.archive/`.
- **Only auto-manages what it created** (`origin: distilled`/`provenance: self-learn`).
- **Never stores secrets.** The fact-extractor drops tokens, cookies, passwords,
  and API keys even if pasted in the open.

## Removal / disable

- Disable the loop only: set `SL_DISPATCH=0` in `~/.claude/self-learn/config.json`
  (`"dispatch_enabled": false`) — the dispatcher then no-ops without touching the
  schedule. Or unregister the scheduled job for your OS (see below).
- Disable one branch: `SL_FACT_NUDGE=0` / `SL_SKILL_NUDGE=0`.
- Full removal — uninstall the plugin via `/plugin`, unregister the scheduler for
  your OS, and (optionally) `rm -rf ~/.claude/self-learn` to discard accumulated
  state/telemetry:
  ```
  # macOS
  launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/ru.secondfry.self-learn 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ru.secondfry.self-learn.plist
  # Linux
  systemctl --user disable --now self-learn.timer 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f ~/.config/systemd/user/self-learn.{timer,service}
  # Windows (PowerShell)
  schtasks /Delete /TN self-learn-dispatcher /F
  ```
